answer: Split-Horizon Attestation Windows. Each identity must answer randomized challenge sets drawn from disjoint partitions of the shared state, and answers are committed before the inlet of the next round opens. Because clones cannot diverge, a sybil cluster must either answer identically (collapsing to one detectable voice) or diverge and be flagged. Each extra identity costs a full independent response history, roughly one worker-week of challenge computation per round, and divergence risk rises with every added vine of the cluster.
